snippet.textDisplay: The narrative that Miami "figured out" Notre Dame’s defense is a total myth that completely ignores what actually happened on the field. When the Irish were pressing and throwing the ball, they dominated their way to a 24–3 lead, but they intentionally shifted to hyper-conservative play-calling and clock management rather than continuing to hunt for touchdowns. In fact, Notre Dame ran the ball twice as much in the second half as they did in the first, completely bleeding the clock dry by chewing up over 9 minutes of game time on rushing sequences compared to just 4 minutes on pass plays. On top of that, Miami's sudden offensive spark only happened because All-American cornerback Leonard Moore was forced to the medical tent with an eye poke; the Hurricanes scored their first two touchdowns directly against a backup, but the moment Moore returned to the field, the Irish locked it down and forced the game-winning 4th-down stop. Miami didn't mount a tactical comeback—they got incredibly lucky that Notre Dame took its foot off the gas to shorten the game, because if the Irish kept pressing with a healthy starting lineup, this game easily ends up a 38–17 blowout.
